title: Participle Clauses
completion_message: ¡Soberbio! Las 'Participle Clauses' son la marca definitiva de un escritor y orador C2. Al usarlas, tu inglés corporativo se vuelve increíblemente conciso, elegante y profesional.

parts.visual:
En inglés avanzado (especialmente escrito), usamos 'Participle Clauses' para combinar oraciones y sonar más concisos y elegantes. Existen tres tipos principales: 

1. Present Participle (-ing): Para acciones simultáneas o causas. 
Normal: Because she was feeling ill, the CEO went home. 
Participle: FEELING ILL, the CEO went home. 
Normal: He walked out of the room and he shouted at everyone. 
Participle: He walked out of the room, SHOUTING at everyone.
parts.audio: Welcome to Participle Clauses. In advanced English, especially in writing, we use participle clauses to combine sentences, making our language more concise and elegant. There are three main types. Number 1: The Present Participle, using the I-N-G form. It's used for simultaneous actions or to show a cause. Normal sentence: Because she was feeling ill, the CEO went home. Participle clause: FEELING ILL, the CEO went home. Another example. Normal: He walked out of the room and he shouted at everyone. Participle: He walked out of the room, SHOUTING at everyone.

parts.visual:
2. Past Participle (3ra columna / -ed): Para voz pasiva o condición. 
Normal: Because it was manufactured in China, the phone is cheap. 
Participle: MANUFACTURED in China, the phone is cheap. 
Normal: If it is handled correctly, this crisis could be an opportunity. 
Participle: HANDLED correctly, this crisis could be an opportunity. 

3. Perfect Participle (Having + participio pasado): Para enfatizar que una acción terminó ANTES que otra. 
Normal: After he had signed the contract, he celebrated. 
Participle: HAVING SIGNED the contract, he celebrated. 
Normal: Because I have seen the report, I know the truth. 
Participle: HAVING SEEN the report, I know the truth.
parts.audio: Number 2: The Past Participle, using the third column or E-D. This replaces a passive voice or conditional phrase. Normal: Because it was manufactured in China, the phone is cheap. Participle: MANUFACTURED in China, the phone is cheap. Normal: If it is handled correctly, this crisis could be an opportunity. Participle: HANDLED correctly, this crisis could be an opportunity. Number 3: The Perfect Participle, using Having plus the past participle. We use this to emphasize that one action finished BEFORE another action began. Normal: After he had signed the contract, he celebrated. Participle: HAVING SIGNED the contract, he celebrated.

questions.question: Normal: Because he knew the truth, he didn't invest. -> Participle: ____ the truth, he didn't invest.
questions.explanation: Present participle (voz activa, causa): Knowing the truth.

questions.question: Normal: After she had finished the presentation, she asked for questions. -> Participle: ____ the presentation, she asked for questions.
questions.explanation: Perfect participle (acción terminada antes que la otra): Having finished.

questions.question: Normal: Because it is located in the city center, the office is expensive. -> Participle: ____ in the city center, the office is expensive.
Normal: He sat at his desk and he drank a cup of coffee. -> Participle: He sat at his desk, ____ a cup of coffee.
Normal: Because I had already read the book, I knew the ending. -> Participle: ____ the book, I knew the ending.
questions.explanation: Perfect participle (acción completada en el pasado): Having read.

questions.question: Normal: If it is viewed from this angle, the problem is obvious. -> Participle: ____ from this angle, the problem is obvious.
questions.explanation: Past participle (condición pasiva): Viewed (Visto desde este ángulo).

questions.question: Normal: As they realized they were late, they ran to the station. -> Participle: ____ they were late, they ran to the station.
Normal: After he had been fired from his job, he started his own company. -> Participle (Pasiva Perfecta): ____ from his job, he started his own company.
questions.explanation: Perfect Participle Passive: Having been fired (Habiendo sido despedido).

questions.question: Normal: Driven by ambition, the manager worked 80 hours a week. -> Participle: ____ by ambition, the manager worked 80 hours a week.
Normal: Not wanting to wake the baby, she walked quietly. -> Participle: ____ to wake the baby, she walked quietly.
questions.explanation: Negación con participios: Not + participio (Not wanting).

questions.question: ____ the email twice, I finally hit send. (Después de haber revisado).
____ in 1998, the company has grown massively. (Fundada).
____ out of the window, he saw the accident. (Mirando).
____ by the sudden noise, the dog started barking. (Asustado).
Not ____ the password, I couldn't log in. (No sabiendo).
____ all his money, he had to borrow from his parents. (Habiendo gastado).
____ carefully, this chemical is safe to use. (Manejado).
She stood there, ____ for him to speak. (Esperando).
____ by a famous architect, the building won an award. (Diseñado).
¿Qué oración es INCORRECTA porque los sujetos no coinciden (Dangling participle)?
options: Walking down the street, the trees looked beautiful.
Walking down the street, I saw beautiful trees.
Having finished the report, she went home.
Exhausted from work, he slept for 12 hours.
questions.correct_answer: Walking down the street, the trees looked beautiful.
questions.explanation: Incorrecta: implica que 'los árboles' estaban caminando. El sujeto de la cláusula principal debe ser el mismo que el de la cláusula de participio.

questions.question: ____ the truth, he stayed silent. (Knowing/Known/Having know)
____ in China, it's cheap. (Making/Made)
____ finished his work, he left. (Habiendo)
____ out the window, I saw her. (Looking/Looked)
____ by ambition, she worked hard. (Driving/Driven)
Not ____ the answer, I guessed. (Knowing/Known)
Having ____ the report, I agree. (Reading/read)
____ correctly, it's safe. (Handled/Handling)
She sat there, ____ coffee. (Drinking/Drunk)
____ founded in 1990, it grew fast. (Being/Been)
